facts.statement: Paraprefica was an extinct potoo that lived during the Middle Eocene, approximately 48 million years ago.
facts.quote: Paraprefica is an extinct genus of potoo (family Nyctibiidae) from the middle Eocene (c. 48 million years ago).

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Paraprefica were discovered in the Messel pit in Germany.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains have been found in the Messel pit at Messel, Germany.

facts.statement: Subsequent research reclassified Paraprefica into the family Nyctibiidae and order Caprimulgiformes based on unique anatomical characteristics.
facts.quote: Later research showed however that Paraprefica had characteristics found only in the family Nyctibiidae, order Caprimulgiformes (the nightjars).

facts.statement: Paraprefica was a medium-sized bird with skull and leg structures resembling those of modern potoos.
facts.quote: Paraprefica, a medium-sized bird, has skull and legs somewhat resembling today's potoos, in the genera Nyctibius and Phyllaemulor.

facts.statement: Paraprefica possessed a thin beak, a very wide mouth, and relatively large wings that were smaller than those of living potoos.
facts.quote: The head has a thin beak and a very wide mouth, while the wings are relatively large, though smaller than those of extant potoos.

facts.statement: Paraprefica is one of the best-preserved Eocene birds, known from complete skeletons and numerous well-preserved skulls.
facts.quote: This bird is known from fossil remains which include a skeleton and many well-preserved skulls, and is one of the best preserved Eocene birds.

facts.statement: Paraprefica lived between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the ancestors of potoos were once cosmopolitan or originally Eurasian, given that Paraprefica fossils are found in Germany while modern species are restricted to the Americas.
facts.quote: The existing finds from Germany present a puzzle on the birds' distribution, as modern potoos are found only in the New World, from Mexico to the north of Argentina and the Caribbean islands of Jamaica, Hispaniola and Tobago, making them Neotropical.

rejected.quote: It is the only known member of the extinct subfamily Parapreficinae, erected in 2021 to distinguish Paraprefica from the extant potoos of the genus Nyctibius and Phyllaemulor.
